items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: For about three years, that's all I did was play with -- around with Jester-Pillars.

ctx.x: joined Jester-Pillars, we had to play like (humming). "Doing the Continental" and all the tunes from "Stormy Weather," all the tunes from the shows. That's what we played. So to play that, you had to play with more quality, you know, Tone. They stressed that.

So when I started playing like that, I forgot about the Roy Eldridges and the Louie Armstrongs, you know. But always my idol -- I didn't completely forget because no one could ever forget Louie Armstrong. But this was a job to me and I was doing my gig. For about three years, that's all I did was play with -- around with Jester-Pillars. And when I went to New York, this is still the same style that I played, you know, in the lower register. And when I joined Basie's band, I still tried to play with this quality,…
